title: Stage 3: The month-end expense report
summary: New-ExpenseReport: from a finance CSV to per-department totals as objects and as an HTML report, with -WhatIf.

steps.title: Finance's monthly ask
body: Every month finance exports `expenses-YYYY-MM.csv` (`Date, Department, Category, Amount, Currency`) and someone
spends an hour in Excel making a table of totals per department. Make it one command that **returns** the totals
(for scripts) and **writes** an HTML report (for people):
Money is **`[decimal]`**, never `[double]`: binary floating point cannot store 0.10 exactly, and the cents drift
across a few thousand rows. And a function named `New-...` that writes a file should support `-WhatIf`

steps.prompt: `ConvertTo-Html -Title 'Expenses' -Head $style` produces a page titled *HTML TABLE*. Why?
options: `-Head` replaces the whole head, including the title: put `<title>Expenses</title>` into the `-Head` text
The style sheet overrides the title
steps.explain: `-Head` and `-Title` do not combine. `-Head "<title>$Title</title>$style"` gives both the title and the styles.

steps.title: New-ExpenseReport: the totals
prompt: and `-Title`. First the data: it must **return** one object per department with **`Department`**, **`Items`** (number
of rows) and **`Total`** (the sum of `Amount` as decimal, rounded to 2 places), biggest total first.

checks.name: the totals per department
checks.fail: Not quite (see what the check found).

hints: `($_.Group | Measure-Object -Property { [decimal]$_.Amount } -Sum).Sum`: a script block as the property converts each amount.
Build `[pscustomobject]@{ Department = $_.Name; Items = $_.Count; Total = [math]::Round(..., 2) }`, sort by `Total` descending, and output the list at the end.
solution: Totals an expense export per department. (The HTML report is still to do.)
steps.explain: Returning the totals *and* writing the file makes the function useful in both worlds: a person runs it and opens the HTML; a script runs it and checks whether any department went over budget.

steps.title: New-ExpenseReport: the HTML report
prompt: Now the report: `New-ExpenseReport` must write `-OutFile` as an HTML page whose **title is `-Title`**, with a table
row per department, and with **`-WhatIf`** it must not write the file (but may still return the totals).

checks.name: the HTML report, and -WhatIf writes nothing
checks.fail: Not quite (see what the check found).

hints: Keep `$totals` as the last line, so it is still returned.
solution: Totals an expense export per department and writes an HTML report. Returns the totals.
$style = '<style>body { font-family: Segoe UI, sans-serif } td, th { padding: 4px 12px; text-align: left } th { background: #eee }</style>'
steps.explain: An HTML file with an inline style sheet survives being attached to a mail, uploaded to SharePoint or opened from a share, which is why it beats a pasted screenshot of Excel. `ConvertTo-Html -Fragment` lets you put several tables (totals, top items, by category) in one page.
